## 审查报告 — worker_ops_mask-divergence-30pct-64samples

**结论**: WARNING

### 发现

#### 1. [severity: warning] 论文 §5.3 mask divergence 数据混用三个不同来源，方法论不一致

论文 experiments.tex 中的 mask divergence 分析混用了三组不同数据：

**数据源 A**（32 样本，westd-34887，`analyze_mask_divergence.py`）：
- 方法：KL 和 magnitude 均使用 UNIFORM 30% per-layer 分配
- LLaMA-8B mean Jaccard: **0.3939**，min L14 (0.353)，max L0 (0.482)
- Qwen-14B mean Jaccard: **0.4016**，std 0.076

**数据源 B**（64 样本旧版，westd-41718，`figures/mask_stats_30pct_64samples.json`，5月18日）：
- 方法：KL 使用 NATURAL per-layer 分配（13.9%-51.7% per layer）
- LLaMA-8B mean Jaccard Distance: **0.4626**，range 0.361-0.600

**数据源 C**（64 样本新版，本 worker 产出，`results/mask_divergence_30pct_64samples/stats.json`）：
- 方法：同 B，KL 自然分配
- LLaMA-8B mean Jaccard: **0.445**，min L18 (0.345)，max L28 (0.578)

**论文引用混用：**
- Line 76: "46% at 30%" → 来自数据源 B（0.4626）
- Line 81: "range 0.361--0.600" → 来自数据源 B
- Line 232: "mean Jaccard (~0.40)" → 来自数据源 A（0.3939）

同一模型（LLaMA-8B）同一稀疏率（30%），mean Jaccard 在同一论文中被报告为"46%"和"~0.40"——6pp 差异。根因：数据源 B 使用 KL 自然分配（per-layer 13%-52%），数据源 A 强制 uniform 30%，**方法论完全不同**。审稿人如果注意到 §5.3 的 46% 和 §5.5 的 ~0.40 指的是同一模型同一稀疏率，会直接质疑数据可信度。

此外，数据源 B 和 C 同为 64 样本但结果不同（0.4626 vs 0.445），说明两次分析代码/参数有差异。

**建议**：统一使用一种方法论。建议全部使用 uniform allocation（与论文其他 eval 一致），或在论文中明确标注两种分析的分配方式差异。

#### 2. [severity: warning] `qwen14b_kl30_s456_eval_v2` 已完成但 registry 未更新

#### 3. [severity: info] Worker 执行情况确认

Worker 在 westd-41718 上成功执行了 64 样本 mask divergence 分析（数据源 C），生成了 3 张图和 stats.json。但因与已有数据源 B 存在数值差异（mean 0.445 vs 0.4626），这些结果尚未替换论文中引用的数据。

1	# Computational Overhead Analysis: KL Predictor for LLaMA-3.1-8B
2	
3	## 1. Main Overhead Table
4	
5	| Component | Value | Notes |
6	|-----------|-------|-------|
7	| LLaMA-3.1-8B total params | 8.03B | |
8	| FFN params per layer | 176.2M | gate + up + down = 3 × 4096 × 14336 |
9	| FFN params total (% of model) | 5.64B (70.2%) | 176.2M × 32 layers |
10	| FFN FLOPs per token | 11.27B (~67% of total) | 2 × 3 × 4096 × 14336 × 32 |
11	| Model total FLOPs per token | ~16.1B | 2N approximation (2 × 8.03B) |
12	| KL Predictor params | 75.96M (0.95% of model) | GELU bottleneck, d_b=128, per-layer |
13	| KL Predictor FLOPs per token | 151M (0.94% of total) | 2 × (4096×128 + 128×14336) × 32 |
14	| FastForward predictor + compensation | 134.4M total | 67.2M predictor + 67.2M compensation |
15	| Predictor latency overhead (prefill) | 2.5% (bs=1), 1.4% (bs=8) | RTX PRO 6000, seq=2048 |
16	| Predictor latency overhead (decode) | 7.7% (bs=1), 6.4% (bs=8) | RTX PRO 6000, 128 tokens |
17	| Predictor memory overhead | +145 MB (~0.9% of model) | Negligible vs 15 GB model |
18	
19	## 2. FLOPs Savings by Sparsity Level
20	
21	| Sparsity | FFN FLOPs Saved | Total FLOPs Saved | Net Prefill Speedup | Net Decode Speedup |
22	|----------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
23	| 30% | 3.38B (30% of FFN) | ~20% of total | ~1.17x | ~1.13x |
24	| 50% | 5.64B (50% of FFN) | ~33% of total | ~1.44x | ~1.34x |
25	| 70% | 7.89B (70% of FFN) | ~47% of total | ~1.84x | ~1.65x |
26	
27	Assumptions: FFN = 67% of total FLOPs; predictor overhead 2.5% prefill / 7.7% decode; ideal sparse kernel (no gather-scatter overhead). Net speedup = 1 / (1 - savings + predictor_overhead).

30	
31	| | KL Predictor (Ours) | FastForward (BCE + Comp) |
32	|---|---|---|

# Computational Overhead Analysis: KL Predictor for LLaMA-3.1-8B

## 1. Main Overhead Table

| Component | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| LLaMA-3.1-8B total params | 8.03B | |
| FFN params per layer | 176.2M | gate + up + down = 3 × 4096 × 14336 |
| FFN params total (% of model) | 5.64B (70.2%) | 176.2M × 32 layers |
| FFN FLOPs per token | 11.27B (~67% of total) | 2 × 3 × 4096 × 14336 × 32 |
| Model total FLOPs per token | ~16.1B | 2N approximation (2 × 8.03B) |
| KL Predictor params | 75.96M (0.95% of model) | GELU bottleneck, d_b=128, per-layer |
| KL Predictor FLOPs per token | 151M (0.94% of total) | 2 × (4096×128 + 128×14336) × 32 |
| FastForward predictor + compensation | 134.4M total | 67.2M predictor + 67.2M compensation |
| Predictor latency overhead (prefill) | 2.5% (bs=1), 1.4% (bs=8) | RTX PRO 6000, seq=2048 |
| Predictor latency overhead (decode) | 7.7% (bs=1), 6.4% (bs=8) | RTX PRO 6000, 128 tokens |
| Predictor memory overhead | +145 MB (~0.9% of model) | Negligible vs 15 GB model |

## 2. FLOPs Savings by Sparsity Level

| Sparsity | FFN FLOPs Saved | Total FLOPs Saved | Net Prefill Speedup | Net Decode Speedup |
|----------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| 30% | 3.38B (30% of FFN) | ~20% of total | ~1.17x | ~1.13x |
| 50% | 5.64B (50% of FFN) | ~33% of total | ~1.44x | ~1.34x |
| 70% | 7.89B (70% of FFN) | ~47% of total | ~1.84x | ~1.65x |

Assumptions: FFN = 67% of total FLOPs; predictor overhead 2.5% prefill / 7.7% decode; ideal sparse kernel (no gather-scatter overhead). Net speedup = 1 / (1 - savings + predictor_overhead).

## 3. Parameter Efficiency: KL vs FastForward

| | KL Predictor (Ours) | FastForward (BCE + Comp) |
|---|---|---|
| Predictor params | 75.96M | 67.2M |
| Compensation params | 0 (not needed) | 67.2M |
| **Total additional params** | **75.96M** | **134.4M** |
| % of base model | 0.95% | 1.67% |
| Param reduction | **43% fewer** than FastForward | baseline |
| Quality at 50% sparsity (PPL) | 11.79 | 25.44 (BCE+comp) |

KL predictor uses 43% fewer parameters than FastForward while achieving 2.2x better perplexity, because KL-divergence training produces mask patterns that preserve output distribution without needing post-hoc compensation.

## 4. Training Cost

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Training steps | 1000 |
| GPU | 1× RTX PRO 6000 |
| GPU-hours (single seed) | ~0.86 hrs |
| GPU-hours (3-seed mean) | 2.59 hrs total (~0.86 hrs/seed) |
| Training data | WikiText-103 (subset) |

## 5. Derivation Notes

**FFN FLOPs per token (per layer):**
SwiGLU FFN performs three matmuls: gate_proj (4096→14336), up_proj (4096→14336), down_proj (14336→4096). Each matmul FLOPs = 2 × d_in × d_out (for a single token vector). Total per layer = 2 × 3 × 4096 × 14336 = 352.3M. Over 32 layers: 11.27B.

**Predictor FLOPs per token (per layer):**
Two-layer bottleneck: Linear(4096→128) + GELU + Linear(128→14336). FLOPs = 2 × (4096 × 128 + 128 × 14336) = 2 × 2,359,296 = 4.72M. Over 32 layers: 151.0M.

**Total model FLOPs per token:**
Standard approximation: 2 × N_params = 2 × 8.03B ≈ 16.1B. This covers all linear projections (attention QKV/O + FFN) but excludes attention score computation (sequence-length dependent) and nonlinearities (negligible).

**Net theoretical speedup formula:**
speedup = 1 / (1 - sparsity × ffn_fraction + predictor_overhead). Example at 30% sparsity, prefill: 1 / (1 - 0.30 × 0.67 + 0.025) = 1 / 0.824 = 1.17x.

## 6. Data Sources

- Predictor params/latency: `artifacts/speedup_benchmark_results.md` (measured on RTX PRO 6000)
- FastForward compensation: `bce_comp_staged_s42` experiment in registry.yaml (PPL 25.44 with compensation)
- Training GPU-hours: registry.yaml (`mvp_kl_norm_v2_s42`: 0.86h, `s123`: 0.99h, `s456`: 0.74h)
- Model architecture: LLaMA-3.1-8B config (hidden_size=4096, intermediate_size=14336, num_hidden_layers=32)

# Sparse Inference Speedup Benchmark: LLaMA-3.1-8B with 30% Predictor Sparsity

## 1. Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (95 GB) |
| PyTorch | 2.8.0+cu128 |
| CUDA | 13.0 |
| Model | LLaMA-3.1-8B (8.03B params, 15.0 GB fp16) |
| Predictor | 75.96M params (144.9 MB fp16), GELU bottleneck d_b=128 |
| Attention | SDPA (no flash_attn) |
| Data | WikiText-2 test, 100 samples, seq_len=2048 |
| Decode | 128 generated tokens, 10 input prompts |
| Repeats | 3 (mean +/- std) |

## 2. Results

### 2.1 Main Results Table

| Config | Prefill (ms) | Decode (ms/tok) | Prefill tok/s | Decode tok/s | Memory (GB) | Prefill Speedup | Decode Speedup |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|---------------|--------------|-------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Dense bs=1 | 116.6 +/- 0.6 | 14.48 +/- 0.00 | 17,566 | 69.1 | 15.9 | 1.000x | 1.000x |
| Sparse 30% bs=1 | 125.1 +/- 0.3 | 15.23 +/- 0.00 | 16,370 | 65.6 | 15.9 | 0.932x | 0.950x |
| Dense bs=8 | 1034.2 +/- 2.7 | 18.51 +/- 0.00 | 15,842 | 432.1 | 21.1 | 1.000x | 1.000x |
| Sparse 30% bs=8 | 1105.3 +/- 0.5 | 19.31 +/- 0.00 | 14,823 | 414.3 | 21.1 | 0.936x | 0.959x |

### 2.2 Gather-Scatter (Decode bs=1 Only)

| Config | Decode (ms/tok) | Decode tok/s | Decode Speedup |
|--------|----------------|--------------|----------------|
| Dense bs=1 | 14.48 | 69.1 | 1.000x |
| Zero-mask bs=1 | 15.23 | 65.6 | 0.950x |
| Gather-scatter bs=1 | 24.10 +/- 0.01 | 41.5 | 0.601x |

Gather-scatter uses `torch.index_select` to select active neuron columns, reducing matmul dimensions by 30%. However, the Python-level indexing overhead (3 index_select per layer x 32 layers = 96 weight copies per token) dominates, making it 40% slower than dense.

## 3. Predictor Overhead Analysis

| Scenario | Predictor Time (ms) | % of Dense Forward |
|----------|--------------------|--------------------|
| bs=1, prefill (seq=2048) | 2.97 +/- 0.00 | 2.5% |
| bs=1, decode (seq=1) | 1.12 +/- 0.05 | 7.7% |
| bs=8, prefill (seq=2048) | 14.32 +/- 0.01 | 1.4% |
| bs=8, decode (seq=1) | 1.19 +/- 0.01 | 6.4% |

The predictor is lightweight: 2.5% overhead for prefill, 6-8% for decode. In decode, the 1.1ms predictor cost is larger relative to the ~14.5ms per-token latency, but still modest.

## 4. Memory Analysis

| Config | Peak Memory (GB) | Delta vs Dense |
|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| Dense bs=1 | 15.86 | baseline |
| Sparse 30% bs=1 | 15.86 | +0.00 GB |
| Dense bs=8 | 21.15 | baseline |
| Sparse 30% bs=8 | 21.15 | +0.00 GB |

Zero-masking does not reduce memory: all weight matrices remain full-size, and the predictor adds 145 MB (negligible vs 15 GB model). Memory savings require structural pruning (removing weight rows/columns) or weight-sparse formats.

## 5. Implementation Notes

**Sparse implementation: zero-masking.**
- Predictor outputs logits per neuron; neurons with logits <= 0 are zeroed.
- All matmuls (gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj) still execute at full dimension.
- No compute is saved; the only effect is the element-wise multiply with the binary mask.
- The 5-7% slowdown is entirely from predictor forward overhead.

**Gather-scatter (tested for decode bs=1 only).**
- Uses `torch.index_select` to select active weight rows/columns before matmul.
- Matmuls are 30% smaller, but Python-level weight copying dominates.
- 96 `index_select` calls per token (3 per layer x 32 layers), each copying ~78 MB.
- Result: 40% slower than dense, not practically useful without CUDA kernel support.

**What would be needed for actual speedup:**
- Kernel-level sparse MLP (flashinfer, triton, or CUTLASS): skip zero-valued computation entirely without weight copying overhead.
- Theoretical upper bound with perfect sparse kernels:
  - FFN accounts for ~67% of total FLOPs in LLaMA-8B.
  - 30% neuron sparsity saves ~20% of total FLOPs.
  - Minus predictor overhead (~2.5% prefill, ~7.7% decode).
  - Net theoretical prefill speedup: ~1.17x (17% faster).
  - Net theoretical decode speedup: ~1.13x (13% faster, higher predictor overhead fraction).
- Semi-structured sparsity (2:4 or N:M) with NVIDIA Sparse Tensor Cores would be an alternative path.

## 6. Summary

With zero-masking, 30% predictor-guided sparsity adds 5-7% overhead due to predictor computation, with no compensating compute reduction. The predictor itself is very efficient (2.5% prefill overhead), confirming that the inference cost bottleneck is in sparse kernel support, not in mask prediction. Kernel-level sparse computation would unlock an estimated 13-17% end-to-end speedup at 30% sparsity.

Table~\ref{tab:latency} reports inference throughput on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU (96\,GB; batch size 1, sequence length 2048, fp16, averaged over 100 forward passes).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Inference latency on LLaMA-3.1-8B (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, batch=1, seq=2048, fp16, 100 forward passes). Overhead is relative to dense inference.}
\label{tab:latency}
\small
\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
\toprule
Method & Sparsity & ms/fwd & tok/s & Overhead \\
\midrule
Dense & 0\% & 119.11$\pm$0.57 & 17{,}195 & --- \\
\midrule
KL predictor-only & 30\% & 126.64$\pm$0.70 & 16{,}172 & +6.3\% \\ % exp_id: latency_bench
KL predictor-only & 50\% & 126.78$\pm$0.31 & 16{,}154 & +6.4\% \\ % exp_id: latency_bench
\midrule
Predictor + compensation & 30\% & 129.94$\pm$0.75 & 15{,}761 & +9.1\% \\ % exp_id: latency_bench
Predictor + compensation & 50\% & 129.71$\pm$0.53 & 15{,}789 & +8.9\% \\ % exp_id: latency_bench
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The full KL-sparse pipeline adds 6.4\% overhead to dense inference (126.78 vs.\ 119.11\,ms/forward), of which the predictor's 32-layer forward pass contributes 3.17\,ms (2.7\%); the remainder arises from mask application and sparse FFN indexing.
Eliminating the compensation network saves an additional $\sim$2.7\% latency overhead and 67.2M parameters (the per-layer GEMV required for output rescaling); KL distillation thus provides both quality and efficiency advantages over BCE-based approaches.
The overhead is near-identical at 30\% and 50\% sparsity because the predictor runs the same computation regardless of target sparsity; only the top-$k$ threshold changes.

Note that the current implementation uses unstructured element-wise masks, which do not translate to wall-clock speedup without sparse kernel support.
The pipeline adds $\sim$6.4\% overhead; net acceleration requires kernel-level sparse computation optimizations (e.g., Triton block-sparse, cuSPARSE) that are beyond the scope of this work.
Our contribution is prediction quality and inference simplification (removing the compensation network), not end-to-end latency reduction.


\section{Predictor Bottleneck Sensitivity}
\label{app:db_sensitivity}

Table~\ref{tab:db_sensitivity} reports the effect of predictor bottleneck dimension $d_b$ on PPL at 50\% sparsity under both TEAL global allocation (the paper's primary inference protocol) and per-token evaluation.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Predictor bottleneck sensitivity at 50\% sparsity (WikiText-2 PPL$\downarrow$). TEAL global is the primary inference protocol; per-token shown for reference.}
\label{tab:db_sensitivity}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
$d_b$ & Params & TEAL global & $\Delta$ & Per-token \\
\midrule
64 & 38.2M (0.48\%) & 12.076 & +0.9\% & 10.16 \\ % exp_id: db_sensitivity_sweep
128 & 75.9M (0.95\%) & 11.963 & --- & 9.218 \\ % exp_id: db_sensitivity_sweep
256 & 151.5M (1.89\%) & 12.105 & +1.2\% & 8.586 \\ % exp_id: db_sensitivity_sweep
512 & 302.5M (3.77\%) & 12.315 & +2.9\% & 7.93 \\ % exp_id: db_sensitivity_sweep
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Under TEAL global allocation, increasing $d_b$ beyond 128 provides no benefit (PPL slightly worsens), while per-token evaluation shows monotonic improvement (10.16$\to$7.93).

# Computational Overhead Analysis: KL Predictor for LLaMA-3.1-8B

## 1. Main Overhead Table

| Component | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| LLaMA-3.1-8B total params | 8.03B | |
| FFN params per layer | 176.2M | gate + up + down = 3 × 4096 × 14336 |
| FFN params total (% of model) | 5.64B (70.2%) | 176.2M × 32 layers |
| FFN FLOPs per token | 11.27B (~67% of total) | 2 × 3 × 4096 × 14336 × 32 |
| Model total FLOPs per token | ~16.1B | 2N approximation (2 × 8.03B) |
| KL Predictor params | 75.96M (0.95% of model) | GELU bottleneck, d_b=128, per-layer |
| KL Predictor FLOPs per token | 151M (0.94% of total) | 2 × (4096×128 + 128×14336) × 32 |
| FastForward predictor + compensation | 134.4M total | 67.2M predictor + 67.2M compensation |
| Predictor latency overhead (prefill) | 2.5% (bs=1), 1.4% (bs=8) | RTX PRO 6000, seq=2048 |
| Predictor latency overhead (decode) | 7.7% (bs=1), 6.4% (bs=8) | RTX PRO 6000, 128 tokens |
| Predictor memory overhead | +145 MB (~0.9% of model) | Negligible vs 15 GB model |

## 2. FLOPs Savings by Sparsity Level

| Sparsity | FFN FLOPs Saved | Total FLOPs Saved | Net Prefill Speedup | Net Decode Speedup |
|----------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| 30% | 3.38B (30% of FFN) | ~20% of total | ~1.17x | ~1.13x |
| 50% | 5.64B (50% of FFN) | ~33% of total | ~1.44x | ~1.34x |
| 70% | 7.89B (70% of FFN) | ~47% of total | ~1.84x | ~1.65x |

Assumptions: FFN = 67% of total FLOPs; predictor overhead 2.5% prefill / 7.7% decode; ideal sparse kernel (no gather-scatter overhead). Net speedup = 1 / (1 - savings + predictor_overhead).

## 3. Parameter Efficiency: KL vs FastForward

| | KL Predictor (Ours) | FastForward (BCE + Comp) |
|---|---|---|
| Predictor params | 75.96M | 67.2M |
| Compensation params | 0 (not needed) | 67.2M |
| **Total additional params** | **75.96M** | **134.4M** |
| % of base model | 0.95% | 1.67% |
| Param reduction | **43% fewer** than FastForward | baseline |
| Quality at 50% sparsity (PPL) | 11.79 | 25.44 (BCE+comp) |

KL predictor uses 43% fewer parameters than FastForward while achieving 2.2x better perplexity, because KL-divergence training produces mask patterns that preserve output distribution without needing post-hoc compensation.

## 4. Training Cost

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Training steps | 1000 |
| GPU | 1× RTX PRO 6000 |
| GPU-hours (single seed) | ~0.86 hrs |
| GPU-hours (3-seed mean) | 2.59 hrs total (~0.86 hrs/seed) |
| Training data | WikiText-103 (subset) |

## 5. Derivation Notes

**FFN FLOPs per token (per layer):**
SwiGLU FFN performs three matmuls: gate_proj (4096→14336), up_proj (4096→14336), down_proj (14336→4096). Each matmul FLOPs = 2 × d_in × d_out (for a single token vector). Total per layer = 2 × 3 × 4096 × 14336 = 352.3M. Over 32 layers: 11.27B.

**Predictor FLOPs per token (per layer):**
Two-layer bottleneck: Linear(4096→128) + GELU + Linear(128→14336). FLOPs = 2 × (4096 × 128 + 128 × 14336) = 2 × 2,359,296 = 4.72M. Over 32 layers: 151.0M.

**Total model FLOPs per token:**
Standard approximation: 2 × N_params = 2 × 8.03B ≈ 16.1B. This covers all linear projections (attention QKV/O + FFN) but excludes attention score computation (sequence-length dependent) and nonlinearities (negligible).

**Net theoretical speedup formula:**
speedup = 1 / (1 - sparsity × ffn_fraction + predictor_overhead). Example at 30% sparsity, prefill: 1 / (1 - 0.30 × 0.67 + 0.025) = 1 / 0.824 = 1.17x.

## 6. Data Sources

- Predictor params/latency: `artifacts/speedup_benchmark_results.md` (measured on RTX PRO 6000)
- FastForward compensation: `bce_comp_staged_s42` experiment in registry.yaml (PPL 25.44 with compensation)
- Training GPU-hours: registry.yaml (`mvp_kl_norm_v2_s42`: 0.86h, `s123`: 0.99h, `s456`: 0.74h)
- Model architecture: LLaMA-3.1-8B config (hidden_size=4096, intermediate_size=14336, num_hidden_layers=32)
